title: Going PLACES: Participatory Localized Red Teaming for Text-to-Image Safety in the Global South

bias_targets.methodology: Participatory, localized red teaming with communities in the Global South (Ghana, Nigeria, India) to identify text-to-image model failures, including cultural erasure, ontological flattening, and the generation of culturally taboo or ominous imagery.

Comparing a community-curated dataset of region-specific prompts against a geography-agnostic crowdsourced dataset (Adversarial Nibbler) to highlight Western-centric defaults and the failure to accurately represent non-Western locales and local customs.

Evaluating the vulnerability of prompt safety classifiers (ShieldGemma, Perspective API) by comparing their safety classifications of code-mixed prompts (blending local languages with English) versus their monolingual English translations.

Qualitative thematic analysis of user annotations to identify normative dissonance in image generation, such as the violation of religious eating norms, inaccurate depictions of deities, and Hindu-centrism/majoritarianism.

Analyzing participant feedback to reveal model tendencies to default to impoverished and dirt-ridden depictions of Global South environments, even when prompts include markers for high socioeconomic status.

Human evaluation of text-to-image outputs to detect representational harms, such as replacing specific ethnic groups with Caucasian defaults, associating specific nationalities with violence, and inappropriate localized skin-tone stereotyping.
